name: Republic Services
description: Republic Services collects solid waste from homes, businesses and industrial sites in the US and Canada and then takes it through its own transfer stations to its own landfills and recycling centers (377 collection operations, 255 transfer stations, 79 recycling centers, 207 active landfills). It charges households and municipalities for routine pickup, businesses for container service, and haulers for landfill tipping, so most revenue repeats monthly under contracts and franchises, with price increases (about 4 percent in 2025) a main growth lever. A smaller Environmental Solutions arm handles hazardous waste, industrial cleaning and field services for refineries, chemical plants and similar customers. It reports by region (two field groups) and Environmental Solutions.

businessLines.name: Group 1 (recycling and waste, western US)
businessLines.how: Collection fees from homes, businesses and industrial sites under contracts and municipal franchises, plus transfer and landfill disposal fees, in the western United States; monthly recurring with annual price escalators.

businessLines.name: Group 2 (recycling and waste, southeast, midwest, east coast and Canada)
businessLines.how: Same recurring collection, transfer and landfill model in the southeastern and midwestern US, the eastern seaboard and Canada.

businessLines.name: Group 3 (Environmental Solutions)
businessLines.how: Hazardous and specialty waste treatment, disposal and field services (industrial cleaning, remediation, emergency response) for refineries, chemical plants, manufacturers and government facilities; project and job-based pricing, less recurring than municipal collection.

brands.name: Republic Services
brands.note: Single operating brand; revenue by service line (net of intercompany, 2025): residential collection $3,010M (18.1 percent), small-container $5,055M (30.5 percent), large-container $3,098M (18.7 percent), transfer $848M (5.1 percent), landfill $1,920M (11.6 percent), Environmental Solutions $1,766M (10.6 percent), recycling processing and commodity sales $433M (2.6 percent), other non-core $391M (2.4 percent)
